name: Introduction and overview — KC-10 Extender — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — KC-10 Extender
description: Introduction and overview of the KC-10 Extender: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history. The KC-10 Extender is a three-engine aerial tanker built by McDonnell Douglas on the DC-10 airframe, entering service in 1981. It combined tanker and cargo roles with the largest fuel capacity of any U.S. tanker. 60 were built; the last retired from U.S. service in 2024. Baseline facts: Three-engine tanker/cargo aircraft; service 1981-2024; 60 built on the DC-10 airframe..
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
key_points: KC-10 Extender: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history.
